device_identification.type: waveguide crossing (4-port intersection, low-loss tapered/lens crossing)
device_identification.reasoning: Silhouette is a 4-fold symmetric flower: four convex petals arranged N/E/S/W with a narrow straight waveguide stub emerging from each petal's outer tip. This is the canonical low-loss waveguide crossing: two perpendicular single-mode waveguides, each locally widened into a biconvex lens/elliptical taper so the mode expands (reducing diffraction/crosstalk) as it passes through the intersection, then re-narrows. The union of the two orthogonal lens tapers produces the 4-petal star with concave notches between adjacent petals. Function: route two waveguides across each other with low insertion loss and low crosstalk.
device_identification.how_it_works: A single-mode guide (width wg_width) adiabatically widens through a symmetric taper to a maximum width (lens_width) at the crossing center, so the field is broad and quasi-collimated where the two guides overlap; this suppresses scattering into the orthogonal port. The taper is roughly elliptical (convex petal edges), re-narrowing to wg_width on the far side. The two orthogonal tapers share the central region.

measurements_from_pixels.notes: thick_y(x) for the horizontal arm: constant 0.236um stub out to |x|~1.84, then grows 0.37->0.54->0.67->0.76->0.84->0.88->0.91 approaching center (ellipse minor half-axis ~0.5um, extrapolated 2b~1.0um at center). Vertical arm identical by 4-fold symmetry.

function_knobs.wg_width: single-mode guide / port-stub width and lens tip width (the guide width)
function_knobs.lens_len: half-length of the elliptical taper along its axis (how far the expansion reaches from center) — the taper length
function_knobs.lens_width: maximum full width of the lens at the crossing center (mode-expansion width)
function_knobs.arm_length_h: through-guide span of the horizontal waveguide (insertion length / footprint)
function_knobs.arm_length_v: through-guide span of the vertical waveguide

verified_knob: arm_length_h (crossing arm through-length); width_um=wg_width; a pure straight so area growth = wg_width*delta is linear and delta_length_um tracks it exactly

iterations.change_made: initial model: two orthogonal through-guides (wg_width straight, full 4.7um span) + two orthogonal elliptical lenses peaking at the crossing CENTER; taper-chain approx of ellipse (rx=1.84, full width 1.0)

remodeled each petal to peak at its MID-radius (lens_len/2) and re-narrow toward both center (lens_center_width) and outer tip (wg_width), producing the concave cusps; recall->1.0 but became a superset (too fat)
shrank uniform oversize halo: lens_len 1.84->1.80, lens_width 1.0->0.92, lens_center_width 0.30->0.22
shifted petal peak inward via lens_peak_frac=0.45 (asymmetric inner/outer semi-lengths) to match measured peak ~0.82um; trimmed outer-flank red + inner-shoulder blue

final width trim lens_width 0.92->0.90; balanced precision 0.989 / recall 0.992. Also set write_gds(with_metadata=False) so the device cell is top-level (measurement-layer gotcha: kfactory $$$CONTEXT_INFO$$$ nesting made _layer_area read 0).

primitives_audit: gf.components.taper (allowed primitive), gf.Path + extrude (through-guides), @gf.cell assembly with add_ref. No gf.components device stencils, no raw polygons.
